land.text: the county of Artois, given as an apanage to Robert on his majority in 1237 under the will of his father Louis VIII

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of France shapes do not cover the Artois cells (0 of 32), so France does not carry a matching loss in the shapes.

land.text: Artois, left in 1330 by Joan II to Joan III with Franche-Comté, who married Odo IV of Burgundy that year

successors.note: Cliopatria's Free County of Burgundy shape of 1333 contains all 32 cells of the last Artois shape; the page has Artois part of the Burgundian ducal house's holdings (1350), then 'part of the Duchy of Burgundy' in 1384.

rulers.name: Robert I
rulers.note: Count of Artois 1237-1250 (succession table); on attaining his majority at twenty-one 'in accordance with the will of his father'; killed at Mansurah on 8 February 1250.

rulers.name: Robert II
rulers.note: Posthumous son and heir of Robert I; killed near Kortrijk on 11 July 1302.

rulers.name: Mahaut
rulers.note: Succeeded her father in 1302 over her nephew Robert III based on 'proximity of blood'; died 1329 (27 November in the infobox, 28 October in a footer).

rulers.name: Joan II
rulers.note: Mahaut's daughter; died 1330. From 1329 the land is drawn by free-county-of-burgundy; Joan II died in 1330 and left Artois and Franche-Comté to Joan III, who married Odo IV of Burgundy that year (County of Artois page; fx-35 moved the end of the drawn state from 1332 to 1329, so Joan III's rule is carried by the Free County dossier).

correction.text: Unchanged shape, to be drawn 1237-1259: Artois, the apanage of Robert I from his majority in 1237

keyframe_review.note: 7,566 km2: Pas-de-Calais (24 of 28 cells) with 8 Nord cells. Infobox: about 4,000 km2 (no year given), ratio 1.9, inside the factor of two; the shape's Nord cells and the coast probably account for the excess. Robert I was count from 1237 ('Count of Artois 1237-1250', Robert I page), so the shape is unchanged but drawn from 1237 to 1259. No page opened dates a change of land in 1241.

7,588 km2, a re-digitisation of the 1241 shape (+22 km2). Robert II, the posthumous son of Robert I, is count from 1250 to 1302; his campaigns (Furnes 1297, Kortrijk 1302) were fought in Flanders and changed no Artois border.

7,610 km2 (+22 km2 against 1260, one Nord cell's worth of geometry). The Treaty of Athis-sur-Orge of 23 June 1305 gave 'Lille, Douai, and Orchies' to the French crown and does not mention Artois or Béthune; Lille lies outside the shape, so the page does not explain the 1305 re-digitisation.

7,610 km2, the same land to 1332. Mahaut died in 1329 and Artois 'passed to her daughter' Joan II; Joan II died in 1330 and left Artois to Joan III, who married Odo IV of Burgundy (1330). No change of land is dated; Cliopatria's Free County of Burgundy shape of 1333 holds all 32 cells. fx-35 (1 Nov 2026): the shape is used 1326-1328 only; Mahaut's death and Artois' passing to the Countess of Burgundy in 1329 end the drawn state (ledger/1), because the Free County of Burgundy dossier draws the same 32 cells from 1329 (hierarchy-fixes: Artois was drawn twice in 1329-1332). [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1326..1328 from this entry's own 'valid 1326-1328 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

region.text: the county of Artois, the apanage of the younger son of Louis VIII

ledger.note: 1237: Robert I becomes Count of Artois. 'in accordance with the will of his father (died 1226) on attaining his majority in 1237 (aged twenty-one)': the apanage of Louis VIII's younger son (County of Artois page: Robert I made count in 1237; 'In 1237, King Louis VIII gave the County of Artois as an…').

region.text: Artois as drawn in the Cliopatria shapes of 1326-1332, taken over by the Countess of Burgundy

ledger.note: 1329: Mahaut dies and Artois passes to the Countess of Burgundy, so the Free County of Burgundy draws it from 1329. 'Upon her death in 1329, Artois passed to her daughter by the Anscarid count Otto IV of Burgundy, Countess Joan II' (County page; death 27 November 1329 in the infobox of the Mahaut page, 28 October in a footer); Joan II 'already held the County of Burgundy'. The state is no longer drawn on its own from this event: free-county-of-burgundy ledger/1 (1329 gain) and keyframe free-county-of-burgundy_1329 already draw the same 32 cells, and Cliopatria draws the personal union as one state from 1333. Joan II died in 1330 and 'bequested Artois and Franche-Comté' to Joan III, who married Odo IV of Burgundy in 1330, tying Artois to the ducal house; Artois reverted to Margaret in 1361 and 'In 1384 all Flanders, Artois and Franche-Comté finally became part of' the Duchy of Burgundy; the county itself goes on (taken by France in 1477, ceded to Philip the Habsburg heir in 1493, back to France on 5 November 1659). fx-35 (1 Nov 2026): the dissolve was dated 1332, the last year of the Cliopatria row, which drew Artois twice in 1329-1332.

wars.name: Franco-Flemish campaigns of Robert II of Artois
wars.outcome: Robert II beat the Flemings at the Battle of Furnes in 1297 and was killed near Kortrijk on 11 July 1302 when his cavalry charge failed on marshy ground; the Treaty of Athis-sur-Orge (23 June 1305) gave Lille, Douai and Orchies to the French crown. No Artois border moved.
wars.note: The Robert II page does not name the war or the Battle of the Golden Spurs explicitly; the County of Artois page has 'the Battle of the Golden Spurs in 1302'. The fighting was in Flanders.

certainty.note: A feudal apanage bounded by Flanders, Boulogne, Ponthieu and Vermandois; no treaty line before 1332 is on the pages (the Treaty of Athis-sur-Orge of 1305 does not mention Artois).

notes: Cliopatria's row ends in 1332 and hands the 32 Artois cells to its 'Free County of Burgundy' row (1333-1384). The county of Artois itself continued: part of the Burgundian holdings 1330-1384, of the Duchy of Burgundy from 1384, taken by Louis XI in 1477, ceded to the Habsburg heir in 1493 (Treaty of Senlis), in the Burgundian Circle from 1512 and French again on 5 November 1659 (County of Artois page): a gap-filler should extend this dossier or write the later Artois (and the Burgundian Netherlands) once the Burgundian groups say who carries it. The Artois succession dispute between Mahaut and her nephew Robert III (after 1302, settled for Mahaut, undated on the pages) and the noble revolts she defeated are undated and have no territorial result. The County of Artois page says Louis VIII gave Artois in 1237 (Louis VIII died in 1226); the Robert I page says 'in accordance with the will of his father' on his majority in 1237, which is followed. The 1305 shape change (+22 km2) is unexplained. Infobox area about 4,000 km2 against Cliopatria 7,566-7,610 km2.
